flags: vcut = -0.1 is negative. Preflight WARN: negative vcut switches EXCLURAD to its alternate 'v' interpretation branch (per the input-file comment) rather than the normal inelasticity-cut (GeV^2) interpretation used by every validated run (default 0.166 for eta). This is not physically impossible and the Fortran will run with it, but it is an unusual/non-standard choice that changes the meaning of the cut, not just its magnitude.
Beam energy defaulted to 6.53 GeV (CLAS12 RG-K campaign, the validated eta source) since none was specified. Other valid CLAS12 energies (10.6, 10.2 GeV) would give different radiative corrections.
explanation: Kinematics (W=1.7 GeV, Q2=1.0 GeV^2, cos(theta*)=0, phi=90 deg) pass all physical checks for the eta channel: W is well above the eta+p threshold (1.4861 GeV), cos(theta*) is away from the +/-1 poles, Q2 is positive and within the lookup-table (W,Q2) coverage, and phi is in range. The only issue is vcut=-0.1, which the user explicitly requested. I generated the input file exactly as specified (vcut=-0.1) rather than silently substituting a positive value, since the user's request was intentional and the negative value is accepted by the Fortran (just interpreted differently, per preflight WARN). Beam energy was defaulted to 6.53 GeV (the RG-K campaign that produced the validated eta reference data); rc_mode was left at the validated default (0 = full O(alpha)).
